title: A strongly cartesian lift of a base pullback square is a pullback
statement: Use the fixed universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with all categories small in the ambient universe. Let $p:\mathcal S\to\mathcal C$ be a functor between categories. Call an arrow $a:s'\to s$ over $u:c'\to c$ strongly cartesian if for every arrow $h:t\to s$ and base arrow $v:p(t)\to c'$ with $p(h)=u\circ v$, there is a unique $k:t\to s'$ with $p(k)=v$ and $a\circ k=h$. Let $f:x\to y$ be strongly cartesian and $g:z\to y$ any arrow. Suppose the base pullback $P=p(x)\times_{p(y)}p(z)$ exists with projections $\pi_x$ and $\pi_z$. Suppose $a:w\to z$ is strongly cartesian with $p(w)=P$ and $p(a)=\pi_z$. There is a unique arrow $b:w\to x$ with $p(b)=\pi_x$ and $f\circ b=g\circ a$. The commutative square with sides $b,a,f,g$ is a pullback in $\mathcal S$: for every $h:t\to x$ and $k:t\to z$ with $f\circ h=g\circ k$, there is a unique $l:t\to w$ with $b\circ l=h$ and $a\circ l=k$. In particular this constructs $x\times_y z$ over the specified base pullback $P$, with strongly cartesian projection to $z$.

proof.text: By the base pullback equation and functoriality, $p(g\circ a)=p(g)\circ\pi_z=p(f)\circ\pi_x$. Apply the strongly cartesian property of $f$ to $g\circ a:w\to y$ and $\pi_x:p(w)=P\to p(x)$. It gives a unique $b:w\to x$ with $p(b)=\pi_x$ and $f\circ b=g\circ a$. Thus the proposed square commutes.

source.place: Tag 06N4, label lemma-strongly-cartesian-fibre-product, proof, construction of b

proof.text: Fix $h:t\to x$ and $k:t\to z$ with $f\circ h=g\circ k$. Applying $p$ gives $p(f)\circ p(h)=p(g)\circ p(k)$. The defining property of the base pullback gives a unique $q:p(t)\to P$ with $\pi_x\circ q=p(h)$ and $\pi_z\circ q=p(k)$. Since $p(a)\circ q=p(k)$, strong cartesianness of $a$ gives a unique $l:t\to w$ with $p(l)=q$ and $a\circ l=k$.

source.place: Tag 06N4, label lemma-strongly-cartesian-fibre-product, proof, first two Hom-set equalities, expanded on a cone

proof.text: The arrows $b\circ l$ and $h$ have the same base map: $p(b\circ l)=\pi_x\circ q=p(h)$. Also $f\circ(b\circ l)=(f\circ b)\circ l=(g\circ a)\circ l=g\circ k=f\circ h$. Uniqueness in the strongly cartesian property of $f$, applied to $f\circ h:t\to y$ and the fixed base map $p(h)$, therefore gives $b\circ l=h$.

source.place: Tag 06N4, label lemma-strongly-cartesian-fibre-product, proof, last Hom-set equality, expanded as uniqueness for f

proof.text: If $l':t\to w$ also satisfies $b\circ l'=h$ and $a\circ l'=k$, then $\pi_x\circ p(l')=p(h)$ and $\pi_z\circ p(l')=p(k)$. Uniqueness for the base pullback forces $p(l')=q$. Now $l'$ and $l$ both lift $q$ and have composite $k$ with $a$, so uniqueness for the strongly cartesian arrow $a$ gives $l'=l$. This proves precisely the pullback universal property in $\mathcal S$. Its projection to $z$ is the given strongly cartesian arrow $a$, and its image object is the specified $P$.
